core_obligations: Use separatedness to build the unique canonical morphism from the spectrum of the second local ring to the scheme (proof lines 12769-12788).
Assume the containment of local rings and construct a second such morphism (proof lines 12790-12801).
Deduce that the second generic point specialises to the first, contradicting the non-containment of the closed subsets (proof lines 12801-12804).
proof_roadmap: Uniqueness of the canonical morphism from separatedness (proof lines 12769-12788).
Contradiction via a second morphism and specialisation (proof lines 12790-12804).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an integral separated scheme the local rings at the generic points of two irreducible closed subsets are distinct subrings of the function field as soon as neither subset contains the other, with the special case that a closed point admits a function regular near it which is outside the other local ring. The proof first uses separatedness to produce a unique morphism from the spectrum of the second local ring to the scheme compatible with the canonical map from the function field, by observing that two candidates agree at the generic point and that the locus where they agree is closed; then, assuming the one local ring were contained in the other, it builds a second such morphism and specialises the two generic points, contradicting the non-containment.
